currentState: Claude Sprout is a public GitHub repository at https://github.com/ZhangZhengruiNUS/claude-sprout.
The app is a Tauri v2 + React + TypeScript + Rust desktop companion for Claude Code.
The primary surface is a transparent, frameless, always-on-top pet window. The full session panel is secondary and opens from the pet or tray.

Tauri v2 Rust backend scaffold
Tray skeleton
Main session panel with mock sessions
PowerShell and Node hook/statusline writers
Local session state model and stale/probably_closed TTL tests

Tauri release exe build support

Interactive pet window: click opens panel, drag moves window through manual setPosition tracking, wheel resizes, right-click enlarges, double-click waves, scale persists in localStorage, transparent background, shadow disabled
Settings persistence under %USERPROFILE%\.claude-sprout\settings.json for do-not-disturb, pet always-on-top, pet lock-position, and pet size
Settings UI controls for small/medium/large pet size, always-on-top, do-not-disturb, and lock-position; changes sync to the live pet window
Vitest test runner with app settings schema tests, plus Rust tests for app-data settings load/save/clamp behavior
Imported pet asset listing from %USERPROFILE%\.claude-sprout\pets plus Settings selection for built-in sprout or imported Codex 8x9 spritesheets
Pet renderer can animate imported Codex 8x9 spritesheets through the Tauri asset protocol while keeping the built-in sprout fallback

Imported Codex pet rendering now matches the Codex/Hatch Pet atlas contract: 8 columns by 9 rows, row-specific frame counts/durations, one-shot rows hold on the final used frame, stable session states map to idle/waiting/running/failed semantics, waiting_input is a weak idle reminder, completion plays jumping once then idles, and scan/import validation rejects non-1536x1872 WebP spritesheets

Codex-compatible pet workflow UI: scan %USERPROFILE%\.codex\pets and %CODEX_HOME%\pets, show valid/invalid candidates with validation errors, import valid candidates, refresh installed pets, and sync imported selections across windows
Animation control polish: one-shot imported sprite rows and built-in jump/failed remount for replay, Settings pet picker previews before applying, and Preview wave exercises the panel pet

Real session refresh foundation: background session-file polling emits refresh events, panel-owned notifications fire for strong waiting_permission/done/error transitions with duplicate suppression after notification delivery, waiting_input remains a weak in-app reminder, permission-denied notifications stay pending for retry, do-not-disturb suppresses notifications, and tray refresh/open data/settings/DND actions are wired

Installer path improvement: default bundle target is NSIS, release scripts separate exe/no-bundle, NSIS installer, and optional MSI/WiX builds, local Tauri installer tools cache under src-tauri\target\.tauri, release doctor reports exact cache files/hashes, and NSIS bundling has generated the local setup exe
Controlled session smoke tooling: npm run smoke:sessions launches the release exe with a temporary CLAUDE_SPROUT_HOME and writes notification/DND transition snapshots

More accurate terminal session handling: Stop, StopFailure, and SessionEnd set ended_at; statusline writers preserve terminal state; Rust derives non-terminal snapshots with ended_at as closed; executable tests cover both PowerShell and Node writers

Manual desktop smoke verified native Windows notifications, DND suppression, tray menu actions, Settings, Open Data Folder, and pet click opening the session panel; pet click now opens/focuses the main window directly with a backend command fallback

Manual release smoke follow-up fixed desktop launch behavior: startup re-hides the main window after window-state restore, tray icon uses the bundled app icon, main-window minimize/close hides to tray, and panel open unminimizes before show/focus

Pet release-smoke polish: tray icon uses a generated tighter 32px sprout icon for better notification-area visibility, and pet right-click opens a context menu with Open, Hide, Activity/Minimal, Larger, and Smaller actions
Pet display mode can now be toggled directly from the pet right-click menu, using the same persisted settings and live resize path as the Settings panel
Pet right-click context menu now closes when the user clicks outside the menu or the pet window loses focus

Pet event actions are now metadata-driven: entering permission-wait states waves once, clean completion jumps once, new errors play failed once, idle-prompt waiting stays weak, and polling/statusline refreshes do not replay actions

Imported Codex pet drag/cropping polish: pet-only window sizing now accounts for 192x208 sprite cells, and imported pet dragging collapses the active surface around the sprite while hiding Activity overlays
Imported Codex sprite bottom clipping is fixed by reserving the unscaled 192x208 cell footprint despite CSS transform scaling, and Activity mode now positions its HUD below imported sprites
Imported Codex Activity mode now reserves unscaled HUD/card height for imported pets, preventing two visible session cards from being clipped below the sprite when pet scale is below 1
Imported Codex pet drag direction now uses runningRight/runningLeft atlas rows while the pet is being dragged horizontally, then returns to the session-driven animation on release

Imported Codex pet dragging now temporarily shrinks the native pet window to the sprite footprint and restores the Activity/Minimal layout on release, preventing the full transparent Activity window from appearing as a square while moving

Idle-prompt input waiting is now a weak reminder: the session remains visible as waiting_input, but it does not trigger native notifications, waiting pet animation, one-shot waving, or actionable counts

Manual release desktop smoke passed after the launch/tray/pet-menu fixes: pet-only startup, visible tray icon, pet menu Open/Hide/Larger/Smaller, minimize/close-to-tray, tray Show/Hide Pet, and tray Quit all behaved as expected
Claude Code hook docs include an empty-session troubleshooting flow for missing hooks/statusLine config, missing sessions/*.json snapshots, and CLAUDE_SPROUT_HOME mismatches
Claude Code hook command examples quote the .ps1 script paths so checkout paths with spaces work; docs call out CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR as the active settings directory override

Frontend Tauri runtime detection accepts globalThis.isTauri as well as __TAURI_INTERNALS__, and Tauri session-load failures no longer fall back to mock sessions so release builds do not show fake Permission needed rows

PowerShell hook/statusline scripts force UTF-8 console input/output before reading Claude Code JSON payloads; executable tests cover CJK assistant text and claude -p verified a real snapshot without hook errors

Session panel diagnostics now expose the active app data root, surface Tauri session-load errors instead of silently showing an empty list, and tolerate malformed historical session snapshots while keeping valid sessions visible

PowerShell hook/statusline session snapshots are now written as UTF-8 without BOM, and the Rust session reader accepts existing BOM-prefixed snapshots so real Windows PowerShell files remain visible in the panel; manual user verification confirmed real sessions display after the fix

Conservative local storage cleanup design is specified at docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-21-storage-cleanup-design.md: Settings owns the Storage entry, safe sessions and old events are cleanable, imported pets are counted but not deleted

Settings Storage cleanup is implemented: storage summary counts sessions/events/pets, safe session cleanup deletes only raw done/error/closed/probably_closed files and keeps running/waiting/idle/stale/unparseable files, old event cleanup deletes only regular files older than 14 days, and imported pets remain read-only

Storage cleanup is preview-bound: frontend sends expected cleanable file count/bytes, Rust rechecks candidates before deleting and rejects stale previews; frontend storage summary loads ignore stale responses; API and StoragePanel tests cover the cleanup request contract and clean-button enablement

Native release smoke for Settings Storage cleanup is complete: the release exe was launched against C:\tmp\claude-sprout-storage-smoke, Storage showed expected cleanable counts, UI cleanup deleted only safe session and old event files, and preserved running/waiting sessions, recent events, event directories, and imported pets

Repeatable installer tool pre-cache workflow: npm run release:precache-tools downloads NSIS, nsis_tauri_utils.dll, and WiX with Node HTTPS, verifies fixed hashes, and populates src-tauri\target\.tauri so Tauri does not depend on the Windows SChannel download path during installer builds

MSI packaging is now validated through the local WiX cache; the bundle icon config points at src-tauri\icons\icon.ico and npm run release:msi generates src-tauri\target\release\bundle\msi\Claude Sprout_0.1.0_x64_en-US.msi
Release artifact policy is documented: the official Windows artifacts are the standalone release exe and NSIS installer, while MSI remains an optional maintainer build behind npm run release:msi

First tagged release checklist is documented at docs/release-checklist.md for v0.1.0 version alignment, tag conflict checks, official artifact builds, SHA256 capture, desktop and installer smoke, unsigned-release notes, GitHub release publishing, and rollback handling

Pet assistant modes are implemented: Minimal mode keeps the compact pet window with glass running/finished/action counts plus actionable message cards; Activity mode expands the pet window for a persistent glass activity stack with highlighted open sessions and pager controls
Pet assistant settings persist across frontend and Rust app-data settings: display mode, completion-card duration where 0 means persist until acknowledged, and visible activity row count

Activity mode cards now show a safer, more distinguishable session identity: Claude rename/session-title metadata when available, otherwise project plus short session id; cards also include metadata-only activity details such as current tool, permission state, status, and context percentage

PowerShell and Node hook/statusline writers preserve display_name across events and can read only Claude transcript summary/title metadata for renamed sessions while avoiding prompt, assistant-output, secret, or project-content capture

Conversation preview reading is now opt-in from Settings: when petConversationPreviewEnabled is true, PowerShell and Node hook/statusline writers read only a bounded tail of the Claude transcript, skip tool_use/tool_result blocks, write a single truncated User/Claude preview into session snapshots, and clear the preview on later writes after opt-out
Activity mode window sizing now supports the default three visible session cards without covering the pet; the 300x364 browser preview leaves visible space between the pet and glass activity panel

Handoff generation no longer embeds live git status/log output because a committed handoff file cannot accurately contain the commit hash that includes itself; sessions now read live Git context at startup

Activity mode conversation previews are more readable: PowerShell transcript reads force UTF-8 and handle single-line transcripts, preview capture stores longer snippets, Activity cards show two preview lines, the Activity window width is configurable, and the pet hover operation hint is removed
Hook/statusline writers tolerate malformed historical session snapshots when preserving display names or terminal state, so a bad old sessions/*.json file no longer causes Claude Code hook errors

Pet message opacity is configurable from Settings and persists as petMessageBoxOpacity; the pet HUD, Minimal message cards, and Activity session cards use CSS variables to adjust glass/card background transparency without dimming text

Activity mode layout now follows the actual open-session count: the HUD is hidden when there are no non-closed sessions, and the pet window height shrinks to the current visible card count instead of reserving the configured maximum rows

Claude Sprout now has a project-standard 3D toy mascot: the built-in pet uses the generated Codex/Hatch 8x9 spritesheet by default, Settings labels it as Claude Sprout, the Vite favicon uses the new mascot PNG, the Tauri bundle icon is regenerated from the same character, and the tray loads a real mascot PNG instead of a hand-drawn placeholder

Local bilingual UI support is implemented without remote services: React uses bundled i18next resources for English and Simplified Chinese, Settings persists a language preference of system/en/zh-CN, Tauri OS locale is used for system language resolution, and Rust tray labels follow the same app setting

Panel settings layout now keeps the left pet preview rail fixed on desktop while the right content area scrolls independently, so pet appearance selection and preview no longer require scrolling back up; narrow screens keep the single-column natural scroll layout

Settings pet appearance now hides the retired imported claude-sprout duplicate after Claude Sprout became the built-in standard pet, and legacy activePetId values for that old import are treated as the built-in selection

Pet window hit testing is tightened: the transparent shell and full compact surface no longer receive pointer events, while a smaller pet-hit-target around the visible pet handles click, drag, wheel, and context-menu interactions; activity/message cards remain individually clickable

Pet dragging now releases cleanly on window-level pointer cancellation, blur, and lost pointer capture, and imported/Activity drag-window shrink anchors to the visible pet-hit-target so the cursor stays on the pet when movement starts

Activity mode now anchors the session stack close below the rendered built-in/imported pet, reserves enough height for three visible cards plus pager, and shows the total active/open session count instead of ambiguous overflow text

Pet assistant user-facing modes are now Message and Board while persisted minimal/activity settings remain compatible: Message mode interrupts only for permission/completion/failure with richer session identity, detail, metadata, and optional conversation preview, while waiting_input remains a weak Board/Session Panel state

Message-mode completion cards no longer reappear on statusline heartbeat refreshes: message identity uses a stable status-event fingerprint instead of updated_at, and acknowledged message keys are pruned once the matching message state is no longer current

README.md and README.zh-CN.md now document the user-facing session status mechanism: Claude Code hook/statusline triggers, stored statuses, Message mode card rules, Board mode visibility/sorting, native notifications, and pet animation behavior

The Windows app/taskbar icon has been regenerated as a DPI-aware multi-size ICO from a tighter mascot crop, with refreshed Vite favicon/project PNGs; the existing tray icon is unchanged because its 32px mascot crop already renders clearly

Idle pet playback is quieter at the renderer level for built-in and imported Codex atlas pets: idle now uses a 4.2-second cycle that holds the first frame for about 2.9 seconds, then plays the remaining idle frames near normal speed to avoid low-framerate stutter; running/waiting/action animations remain unchanged
Pet resizing now supports smaller sizes: the shared frontend/Rust minimum pet scale is 0.55, and the Settings small preset uses 0.65 while keeping medium and large unchanged

Message-mode HUD badges now follow smaller atlas pets with a small breathing gap: the running/finished/action pill row uses a measured bottom offset based on the sprite frame height and pet scale instead of staying fixed to the reserved window footprint

Do Not Disturb is now treated as a normal Settings notification toggle instead of a topbar priority action; its description clarifies that only Windows system notifications are suppressed while pet cards, Board, and session state remain visible

Session panel appearance has a persisted system/light/dark theme setting next to Language in Settings; the panel now uses light and dark glass/acrylic design tokens with translucent rails, panels, controls, segmented buttons, and session/storage rows while preserving the pet window's transparent route

The session panel no longer has the large top hero/title band; content now starts with the compact local status strip followed by the current Sessions or Settings surface, keeping the panel focused on settings and detailed Claude Code session inspection rather than dashboard-style presentation

The release exe build works with npm run release:exe or npm run tauri -- build --no-bundle, and the NSIS installer build works while the verified local NSIS cache is present.

importantDecisions: Do not make the product a browser-style dashboard. The pet window is the first-class UI.
Do not auto-approve Claude Code permission prompts.
Keep prompts/outputs out of stored state by default.
PowerShell hook writer is the default for Windows; Node hook writer remains a fallback.
Imported Codex-compatible pet assets are copied into Claude Sprout app data; do not reference or distribute official Codex assets.
The standard built-in pet and app/tray icons should use the generated Claude Sprout mascot assets checked into the project, while imported pets remain optional user-selected alternatives.
Codex-compatible imported pets use the Codex/Hatch Pet 8-column by 9-row atlas contract; unused cells remain transparent and should not be stepped through during playback.

Conversation preview is an explicit local opt-in. Default behavior stays metadata-only; when enabled, writers may store only a single truncated User/Claude transcript snippet in sessions/*.json and must not append prompt/output snippets to events/*.jsonl.

User-facing pet assistant modes are Message and Board: Message mode is low-frequency rich-context intervention for permission/completion/failure, Board mode is the persistent multi-session stack, and waiting_input remains a weak non-interrupting state.
Message-card deduplication should be based on the logical status event, not statusline heartbeat updated_at; heartbeat refreshes must not create fresh completion/error/permission cards.
The README session status sections are the user-facing source of truth for hook/statusline triggers and Message/Board behavior; update README.md and README.zh-CN.md whenever those rules change.

Bilingual support stays local and low-noise: no remote localization service, bundled English/Simplified Chinese resources, language preference persisted in app settings, and system locale detection only when language is set to system.
Official Windows release artifacts are the standalone release exe and NSIS installer; MSI remains an optional maintainer build, not a required release artifact.
